replicate_statements: Distribution of SMF-derived promoter state frequencies as a function of Pol II ChIP-seq level in Drosophila promoters (n = 5912 promoters).
Promoters were first binned based on their log2 Pol II ChIP-seq signal. Within each bin, the median frequency of each of the promoter state was calculated.
outputs.explanation: The panel reports median state frequencies computed across a defined number of promoters (n = 5912), with promoters explicitly named as the replicate/sample unit.

replicate_statements: Each row in the single-molecule stack denotes a single DNA molecule and the methylation status of each cytosine in that molecule.
Pol II - 17%, PIC - 54% (percentages derived from the molecule stack)
outputs.explanation: The panel states the number of molecules (2952) analyzed for this single-locus example and identifies molecules as the replicate unit used to derive the state percentages shown.

replicate_statements: Distribution of SMF-derived state frequencies as a function of Pol II ChIP-seq level in mouse promoters (n = 6122 promoters).
outputs.explanation: The panel reports n = 6122 mouse promoters as the replicate/sample unit for the median state frequency distributions, matching panel A's approach.

replicate_statements: Single-locus example of a single-molecule sorting of a highly active, TATA-box containing mouse promoter (Skp1, 97th percentile by Pol II ChIP-seq). Same representation as (B).
Pol II - 9%, PIC - 48% (percentages derived from the molecule stack)
outputs.explanation: The panel states the number of molecules (2871) analyzed and molecules are named as the unit underlying the reported state percentages.

replicate_statements: Comparison of PIC state frequency between mouse (TATA-less n = 572 promoters; TATA-containing n = 64 promoters) and Drosophila (TATA-less n = 422 promoters; TATA-containing n = 71 promoters) promoters.
Boxplots represent the distribution of the frequency of PIC-bound molecules ... at highly active promoters (top 5% Pol II ChIP-seq level).
The statistical comparisons between groups were performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
outputs.explanation: Group-specific n-numbers (promoters) are explicitly given for all four boxplot groups, and the statistical test used is named; smallest n (64) is well above the minimum threshold for summary statistics.
